sentences.text: Turfanosuchus is an extinct genus of archosauriform reptile, a name that translates to "Turfan basin crocodile".
This animal possessed teeth located on its palate and internal carotid arteries that entered the braincase from below.
The premaxilla of the skull projects a small prong situated behind the nostrils.
Additionally, the maxilla features a rare posterodorsal process.
The upper jaw likely held five teeth in the premaxilla and at least thirteen in the maxilla.
Preserved specimens show that these teeth were curved and finely serrated.
The lower jaw contained at least sixteen teeth.
Among gracilisuchids, Turfanosuchus is unique because its lower jaw prong is much longer than the upper prong.
The outer surface of the surangular bone is highly concave, a trait not seen in other relatives.
Although initially thought to lack them, one osteoderm was later found on the skeleton.
The heel bone shares many similarities with those of crurotarsan archosauriforms.
Like other diapsids, Turfanosuchus had two openings at the rear of its skull known as temporal fenestrae.
The genus Turfanosuchus was described by C.C. Young in 1973.
The type species T. dabanensis was based on a partially complete, disarticulated skeleton found in the Kelamayi Formation of the Turfan Basin.
This specific fossil, catalogued as IVPP V.32237, was the basis for the original description.
The fossil was not fully prepared at the time of the initial description.
In 2001, Xiao-Chun Wu and Anthony Russell redescribed the fossil.
Further preparation revealed a partial osteoderm.
The parent group of Turfanosuchus is Gracilisuchidae.
Turfanosuchus belongs to the family Gracilisuchidae.
The type species of the genus Turfanosuchus is Turfanosuchus dabanensis.
There is one recorded fossil occurrence for the genus Turfanosuchus.
Turfanosuchus is likely a member of the family Gracilisuchidae within the archosaurs.
A 2014 study grouped Turfanosuchus with Gracilisuchus and Yonghesuchus in the family Gracilisuchidae.
Turfanosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic (Anisian) in northwestern China.
The animal lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically the Anisian stage, approximately 240 to 237 million years ago in what is now China.
Wu & Russell (2001) classified Turfanosuchus as a non-archosaur archosauriform based on its pterygoid teeth.
Recent findings of pterygoid teeth in other crown-archosaurs suggest Turfanosuchus may be a crown-archosaur.
